definition: A concept is what the topic is an example of: a 2-4 word transferable phrase that transfers across at least 3 disciplines, connects to the student's own life, recurs across units and years, and carries a wisdom layer (an uncomfortable personal question).

mistakes.name: Naming the topic as the concept
mistakes.example: The concept of this unit is the Industrial Revolution.
mistakes.fix: The Industrial Revolution is the unit; the concept is Innovation and Transformation.

mistakes.name: Going too broad
mistakes.fix: A concept that excludes nothing explains nothing.

mistakes.name: Going too narrow
mistakes.fix: It only lives inside the Industrial Revolution and does not transfer.

mistakes.name: No wisdom layer
mistakes.fix: The personal question 'be innovative!' is shallow; go deeper until the question is uncomfortable.

mistakes.name: Different concepts for units that share one
mistakes.example: Power and Legitimacy fits Turkish Invasions, WWI and Colonial Imperialism.
mistakes.fix: That is the point: concepts recur and build.

four_checks: Can AI give a definitive answer? (It must not.)
Does it transfer across three disciplines?
Would a student need this concept to complete the PoC?

crit.context: I am a teacher at an IB school. I am planning a unit and I need help identifying the transferable concept - the big idea - that sits underneath my topic. I am not looking for a topic description. I am looking for the deeper principle that this topic is an example of, which can transfer across at least three other disciplines and connect to students' personal lives.
crit.role: Act as an expert curriculum designer with deep knowledge of concept-based learning, the IB framework, and interdisciplinary education. You understand the difference between a topic (what students study) and a concept (what the topic is an example of).
crit.interview: Before giving me any suggestions, interview me. Ask me one question at a time - up to three questions - to understand my unit, my students, and what I want them to walk away understanding about the world.
crit.task: Based on my answers, suggest three possible concepts for this unit - each expressed as a 2-4 word transferable phrase. For each concept, tell me: (1) what other disciplines it appears in, (2) what personal wisdom question it generates for students, and (3) what would make it the wrong concept to choose.
